침대.x: There is a big bed in my room.

거울.x: I look in the mirror every morning.
거울.t: 'Look in the mirror' = 거울을 보다 (object particle, no 'in').

주문하다.x: I ordered two coffees and a cake.
주문하다.e: Literally 'noting in writing' — picture a waiter writing down your order.
주문하다.t: Waiters ask: 주문하시겠어요? 'Are you ready to order?'

내려오다.m: to come down, to come downstairs
내려오다.x: My legs hurt when I came down the mountain.
내려오다.e: 내리다 (to go down) + 오다 (to come): come down toward the speaker.
rel: to get off, to go down

점수.ex: 이번 시험에서 점수가 생각보다 잘 나왔어요.
점수.x: My score on this test came out better than I expected.

돌려주다.x: I'll give back the book I borrowed by tomorrow.
돌려주다.e: 돌리다 'to turn' plus 주다 'to give' — turning it back to the owner.

힘내세요.m: cheer up; hang in there; you can do it
힘내세요.ex: 내일 시험이 있죠? 너무 걱정하지 말고 힘내세요!
힘내세요.x: You have an exam tomorrow, right? Don't worry too much — you've got this!
힘내세요.e: 힘 'strength' plus 내다 'bring out': literally 'bring out your strength'.

가난하다.x: He was very poor when he was young.
가난하다.e: From older 간난 'hardship'; the sound softened to 가난 over time.

얘기.ex: 어제 친구랑 재미있는 얘기를 많이 했어요.
얘기.x: Yesterday I talked about a lot of fun stuff with a friend.
얘기.t: 얘기 is casual and spoken; 이야기 is preferred in writing.

연세.x: Excuse me, but how old is your grandfather?
연세.e: Literally 'years and age'; the respectful word for an elder's age.
연세.t: Use 연세 instead of 나이 for elders: 연세가 어떻게 되세요? is the polite way to ask.

차례.m: turn; order, sequence; table of contents
차례.x: Next is Minsu's turn. Please get ready.
차례.t: Don't confuse it with the homonym 차례 meaning the holiday ancestral rite on Seollal and Chuseok.

차례.ex: 추석 아침에 가족들이 모여서 차례를 지내요.
차례.x: On Chuseok morning, the family gathers to hold the ancestral rite.
차례.t: Homonym: 차례 also means 'turn, order' (제 차례예요 'It's my turn'); for the rite say 차례를 지내다.

조언.ex: 취업 준비에 대해 교수님께 조언을 구했어요.
조언.x: I asked my professor for advice on job hunting.
조언.t: Common pairs: 조언을 구하다 (ask for advice) and 조언을 해 주다 (give advice).

소극적.ex: 저는 처음 만난 사람 앞에서 좀 소극적이에요.
소극적.x: I'm a bit reserved around people I've just met.
소극적.e: Opposite of 적극적: 'fading from the extreme'.

기본.x: In Korea, greeting people is the most basic part of good manners.

엔지니어.x: My friend is an engineer at a car company.

대출하다.m: to lend, to borrow (a loan); to check out (library books)
대출하다.x: I took out a loan from the bank to buy a house.
대출하다.t: Borrowers often say 대출을 받다 'get a loan'; at libraries, 책을 대출하다 means checking out books.

음주.ex: 음주 후에는 절대 운전하면 안 돼요.
음주.x: You must never drive after drinking.

탈퇴하다.m: to withdraw, to quit (a group or membership)
탈퇴하다.ex: 요즘 사용하지 않는 사이트에서 모두 탈퇴했어요.
탈퇴하다.x: I withdrew from all the sites I don't use these days.
탈퇴하다.t: Common patterns: 회원 탈퇴 'delete account' and 동아리에서 탈퇴하다 'leave a club'.

보존.ex: 문화재 보존을 위해서 사진 촬영이 금지되어 있습니다.
보존.x: Photography is prohibited to preserve cultural heritage.
보존.e: Literally 'protecting so it continues to exist.'
보존.t: For files on a computer, use 저장, not 보존.

만일.m: if, in case; an emergency, the unlikely event
만일.ex: 만일 비가 오면 소풍은 다음 주로 미룰게요.
만일.x: If it rains, we'll push the picnic back to next week.
만일.e: Literally 'one in ten thousand' — a slim chance.
만일.t: Interchangeable with 만약; 만일의 경우에 대비하다 means 'to prepare for the worst case.'

발휘하다.m: to display, to show (ability), to exert
발휘하다.x: That athlete showed his true skill in the final.
발휘하다.e: Literally 'send out and wield' your abilities.

빨대.x: Could I get a straw for the iced americano?
빨대.e: Native word: 빨다 'to suck' + 대 'stick, tube'.
빨대.t: Pronounced [빨때]. Many Korean cafés now hand out paper straws (종이 빨대) instead of plastic ones.

아삭아삭.x: The cucumber is fresh, so it's nice and crunchy.
아삭아삭.e: Sound word (의성어) for biting into something fresh and juicy, like cucumber, apple or kimchi.
아삭아삭.t: Pronounced [아사가삭]: the ㄱ links to the next vowel. 아삭하다 is common: 아삭한 김치 'crisp kimchi'.

만큼.forms: Same form after any noun: 형만큼 · 이만큼 · N만큼 …지 않다 (not as … as N)
만큼.x: Seoul wasn't as cold as I thought.
만큼.e: Native word. After verbs it's a bound noun written with a space: 먹을 만큼 'as much as you'll eat'.
만큼.t: 노력한 만큼 결과가 나와요 'You get results in proportion to your effort' — a very common use after verbs.

노동조합.x: The employees decided to form a labor union.
노동조합.e: Literally 'labor association' — workers combined into one group.

전임.x: The former department head moved to another branch.
전임.t: A different 전임 means 'full-time', as in 전임 강사 (full-time lecturer).

대안.ex: 자동차 대신 자전거가 좋은 대안이 될 수 있어요.
대안.x: Bikes can be a good alternative to cars.

호전되다.m: to improve, to take a turn for the better (health, situation)
호전되다.ex: 약을 바꾼 후로 증상이 많이 호전됐어요.
호전되다.x: Since I changed medication, my symptoms have improved a lot.
호전되다.t: Formal; in conversation people usually say 좋아지다 instead.

재발.ex: 허리 통증이 재발해서 다시 병원에 갔어요.
재발.x: My back pain came back, so I went to the hospital again.

선율.ex: 이 곡은 선율이 아름다워서 자주 들어요.
선율.x: This piece has a beautiful melody, so I listen to it often.
선율.e: Literally 'circling tones'; a more literary word than 멜로디.
선율.t: Pronounced [서뉼]; the ㄴ links over, and 률 becomes 율 after a ㄴ batchim.

난처하다.m: awkward, embarrassing, in a difficult position
난처하다.ex: 두 친구가 동시에 부탁해서 정말 난처했어요.
난처하다.x: Two friends asked me for favors at the same time, so I was in a real bind.
난처하다.t: Common pattern: 난처한 입장에 처하다 'to be put in an awkward position'.

호감.ex: 처음 만났을 때부터 그 사람에게 호감이 있었어요.
호감.x: I've liked that person since we first met.
호감.t: 호감이 가다 'to be drawn to'; 호감형 means 'a likable type', often said of faces.

순수하다.x: I really love children's pure hearts.

겸손.x: Humility is a very important virtue in Korea.
겸손.t: Answering praise with 아니에요 is a common, expected show of 겸손 in Korea.

내내.forms: time + 내내 (여름 내내, 일 년 내내); 내내 + verb
내내.m: all along, throughout, the whole time
내내.x: I did nothing but play games at home the whole vacation.

여태.forms: 여태 + negative/past: 여태 안 왔어요? 여태 뭐 했어요?
여태.x: You still haven't done your homework?
여태.e: Means the same as 이제까지 'up to now'.
여태.t: Often carries mild surprise or blame: 여태 자고 있었어요? 'You were sleeping until now?'

전념하다.m: to devote oneself, to concentrate on
전념하다.x: He quit his job and devoted himself to research.

추가하다.x: Please add a little milk to my coffee.
추가하다.t: Very common when ordering: 샷 추가해 주세요 = an extra shot, please.

매달리다.m: to hang (from), to dangle; to cling to; to beg; to be devoted to
매달리다.ex: 아이가 엄마 팔에 매달려서 떼를 썼어요.
매달리다.x: The child hung on Mom's arm and threw a tantrum.
매달리다.e: Passive of 매달다 'to hang', from 매다 'to tie' + 달다 'to hang'.
매달리다.t: Figurative: 일에 매달리다 means to be glued to one's work.

부추기다.m: to egg on, incite, stir up
부추기다.ex: 친구들이 옆에서 두 사람의 싸움을 부추겼어요.
부추기다.x: Our friends egged on the fight between the two of them.
부추기다.e: Unrelated to 부추 'garlic chives', despite the look-alike spelling.

휘두르다.forms: 휘둘러요 · 휘둘렀어요 · 휘두를 거예요 · 휘두르세요 (르 irregular)
휘두르다.m: to swing, wield; to push (people) around
휘두르다.x: He got angry and swung his fists.
휘두르다.t: The passive 휘둘리다 means 'to be swayed or pushed around' by someone.

통행료.x: I usually pay highway tolls with Hi-pass.
통행료.e: Literally 'fee for passing through.' -료 = fee: 입장료, 수수료.

포인트 안무.ex: 이번 노래는 포인트 안무가 쉬워서 다들 따라 해요.
포인트 안무.x: The signature move of this song is easy, so everyone copies it.
포인트 안무.t: Usually the catchy move in the chorus (후렴) that fans copy.

비틀비틀.x: A drunk man is staggering along.
비틀비틀.e: 의태어 (manner word) for walking unsteadily, swaying as if about to fall.
비틀비틀.t: Typical causes are drinking, dizziness or exhaustion. The verb is 비틀거리다.

민심.ex: 선거 결과는 민심을 그대로 보여 줍니다.
민심.x: Election results show public sentiment just as it is.

견제.x: The opposition party plays the role of keeping the government in check.
견제.t: 견제와 균형 means checks and balances; in sports, 견제 is guarding against a rival.

위임.x: The CEO delegated decision-making authority to the vice president.

보건.ex: 정부는 국민 보건을 위해 새로운 정책을 발표했습니다.
보건.x: The government announced a new policy for public health.
보건.t: 보건 is institutional (public health); for a person's own health, use 건강.

산재하다.m: to be scattered, to be dotted about
산재하다.ex: 이 지역에는 오래된 유적이 곳곳에 산재해 있어요.
산재하다.x: Old ruins are scattered all over this region.
산재하다.t: Usually in the -해 있다 form; figuratively, 문제가 산재해 있다 = problems are everywhere.

비일비재.m: very common, happening all the time
비일비재.x: These days, scams like this happen all the time.
비일비재.e: Literally 'not once, not twice' — again and again.

감언이설.ex: 나이 드신 분들은 사기꾼의 감언이설에 속기 쉬워요.
감언이설.x: Elderly people are easily fooled by con artists' sweet talk.

유일무이하다.ex: 이 그림은 세상에 하나뿐인 유일무이한 작품이에요.
유일무이하다.x: This painting is a one-of-a-kind work, the only one in the world.

기미.ex: 비가 그칠 기미가 전혀 보이지 않아요.
기미.x: There's no sign at all of the rain stopping.
기미.e: Literally 'slight and minute': a faint first hint. Homonym 기미 = dark facial spots.
기미.t: Typical pattern: ~(으)ㄹ 기미가 보이다/없다 (show signs of ~ / no sign of ~).

부풀리다.m: to inflate, blow up; to exaggerate
부풀리다.x: Some media outlets greatly exaggerated the incident.
부풀리다.e: Causative of 부풀다 'to swell, puff up'.

금고.x: He was sentenced to one year of imprisonment without labor for professional negligence.
금고.e: Literally 'confine and shut in'; the homonym 금고 means 'safe, vault'.
금고.t: 징역 includes prison labor; 금고 is confinement only, often given for negligence crimes.

수뢰.x: The former mayor was arrested on charges of taking bribes.

사유재산.ex: 민주 국가의 법은 개인의 사유재산을 보호합니다.
사유재산.x: The laws of democratic countries protect individuals' private property.

신용불량.ex: 카드값을 못 갚아서 신용불량 상태가 됐어요.
신용불량.x: I couldn't pay my credit card bills, so I ended up with bad credit.
신용불량.t: Most often heard as 신용불량자, a person blacklisted for unpaid debts.

비례대표.ex: 그는 지난 선거에서 비례대표로 국회의원이 되었습니다.
비례대표.x: He became a lawmaker through proportional representation in the last election.
비례대표.e: Literally 'representation by ratio' — seats follow each party's share of votes.

계엄.x: The government declared martial law, citing a state of emergency.
계엄.t: Pronounced [계엄] or [게엄]; collocations: 계엄을 선포하다 (declare), 계엄을 해제하다 (lift).

귀납법.ex: 과학자들은 실험 결과를 바탕으로 귀납법을 활용해요.
귀납법.x: Scientists use inductive reasoning based on experimental results.

연호.x: King Gwanggaeto used his own era name, Yeongnak.
연호.e: Literally 'year name' — monarchs named eras to count years.
연호.t: Japan still uses era names today, such as 레이와 (Reiwa).

호도하다.m: to gloss over, to misrepresent, to mislead
호도하다.ex: 정부가 사실을 호도하고 있다는 비판이 나왔습니다.
호도하다.x: Criticism arose that the government was misrepresenting the facts.
호도하다.e: Literally 'paste and smear' — plastering over the truth.
호도하다.t: Common collocations: 사실을 호도하다 and 여론을 호도하다 'to mislead public opinion'.

안이하다.ex: 문제를 너무 안이하게 생각하면 안 돼요.
안이하다.x: You shouldn't think about the problem so complacently.
안이하다.e: Literally 'comfortable and easy' — too relaxed about something serious.
안이하다.t: Critical in tone: 안이한 대처 'a complacent response'; don't confuse with 용이하다 'easy to do'.

인구구조.ex: 인구구조의 변화는 경제에 큰 영향을 미칩니다.
인구구조.x: Changes in population structure have a big impact on the economy.
인구구조.e: Literally 'population construction': the age and gender makeup of a society.

추대하다.m: to elect or install (someone as leader), to set up as head
추대하다.x: The members unanimously installed him as president.
추대하다.e: Literally 'push up and hold overhead' — raising someone to lead.

간교하다.ex: 그는 간교한 꾀로 순진한 사람들을 속였어요.
간교하다.x: He deceived innocent people with crafty tricks.

순진무구.m: pure and innocent, without a trace of guile
순진무구.x: The child's pure, innocent smile warmed my heart.
순진무구.t: Most often as an adjective: 순진무구하다, 순진무구한 눈빛.

필부필부.m: ordinary men and women, common folk
필부필부.ex: 역사를 움직이는 것은 결국 필부필부의 힘입니다.
필부필부.x: In the end, it is the strength of ordinary people that moves history.
필부필부.e: Literally 'an ordinary husband and an ordinary wife.'
